title: Tech 02 Api Rate Limits
decision: Choose an API rate-limiting architecture for a multi-tenant SaaS API.
context: Traffic is bursty and tenants range from tiny accounts to large integrations.
The API runs in three regions behind active-active routing.
constraints: The limiter must prevent one tenant from exhausting shared capacity.
A regional network partition must not stop all requests.
Operational complexity must fit a five-person platform team.
options: A single globally centralized limiter service.
Per-instance in-memory token buckets with no cross-instance coordination.
Regional token buckets with bounded global quotas and local burst allowance.

evidence.fact: The top 2 percent of tenants generate 61 percent of request volume during peak hours.
Observed bursts frequently reach 4 times a tenant's five-minute average for less than 20 seconds.
Cross-region control-plane round trips have a p99 latency of 180 ms.
A prior regional dependency outage lasted 11 minutes while application instances in the region remained healthy.
Platform on-call currently supports eight shared services and has budget for at most one new stateful dependency.
Tenant entitlement data is already replicated regionally and can provide per-tenant quota inputs without a new global lookup.
